concepts.def: A fundamental particle (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) that makes up hadrons.
A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).
A neutron decays to a proton, electron and antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
In particle interactions, charge, baryon number, lepton number and energy/momentum are conserved.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Particles & Medical Physics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Particles & Medical Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Particles & Medical Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: udd
uud
uds
uuu

mcqs.q: In β⁻ decay, the exchange particle is:
options: Photon
W⁻ boson
Gluon
Z boson

mcqs.q: Is the proton a fundamental particle?
options: It is a proton that has lost its charge.
No — protons are made of electrons.
No — it is made of two up quarks and one down quark; the electron, by contrast, is fundamental.
Yes — protons cannot be broken down any further.

mcqs.q: In beta-minus decay, where does the emitted electron come from?
options: It is a proton that has lost its charge.
It is one of the atom's orbital electrons knocked out of its shell.
A neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton, creating an electron and an antineutrino.
No — protons are made of electrons.

mcqs.q: Are X-rays and gamma rays fundamentally different kinds of radiation?
options: Yes — gamma rays are particles while X-rays are waves.
No — both are high-energy electromagnetic radiation; they differ mainly in origin (atomic/tube processes versus the nucleus).
It is a proton that has lost its charge.
Yes — X-rays are a form of sound wave.
